notes.title: Synthetica 0.7.0 is live!
notes.content: [p]Hi there, long time no see! :D[/p][p]So, [b]Synthetica version 0.7.0[/b] is live. Yay! But let's start from the beginning.[/p][p]Version 0.6.0 was published at the end of February, followed by some minor updates in March. The game was okay, still too many features were incomplete, and the overall experience was, well, not very inspiring. We also started to have a lot of internal conflicts in our small team, because of the differences in the game vision (which, from my side, hasn't changed since the start of the project). And then The Crunch Time at my workplace slowed everything even more. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44897959/8898c047353b25cd637d23e957f06652374c7339.jpg"][/img][/p][p]So, by the end of March, I was a solo indie developer again with an increased workload and a list of over 100 things and features to design, implement, balance, and so on. It was a massive overscope for a single person. I had a lot of mixed feelings about the situation and considered various options. But after thorough consideration and a few dives into "let's cancel everything, it's impossible to make in an adequate amount of time", I found a kind of compromise solution.[/p][p]I opened my Google sheet with plans and began cutting everything. It's cool to have Boosters, which will give your workers time-based bonuses. And the News system with world events sounds nice. And the Perk Modules, which you can buy or craft and insert into your androids to give them the permanent unique abilities - sure, why not now. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44897959/2d8c2951c8bc94f2ef2660acdf8947630a14c8be.jpg"][/img][/p][p]But if you have a few free hours per week, even being quite an experienced developer and designer, it still would take months (more than 12) to finish everything in a decent state. And the game won't be fully playable until everything is implemented - that was the suspicious part. [/p][p]So, I made everything simpler, both for the implementation and for UX. The core is still here - you craft android workers, match them with clients, earn money and rating, upgrade your club, research stuff, and help your clients through the dialogue events. But a lot of things became more distilled, if I can use that word. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44897959/c0acd5313040b1002d754849c64d6a8e6bf0029b.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Some secondary resources were combined to simplify everything. No more separate Research Points, for example - now you can use your money to buy the new technologies and upgrades. Sure, it's a simplification, but at the same time, it solves a lot of issues with progression and economics.[/p][p]Another example is the Android Deconstruction System. Sure, it was great on paper - you can deconstruct your androids, get some random, leveled-up part from it, and some scrap parts, and craft the new, improved android from them. And there was a strict request for an AI Module that controlled the number of androids. And some hardware and software upgrade modules which can be inserted, or which you could get from the disassembly. [/p][p]You already see where this is going. It's a lot of things. And when you think about it one more time, you can leave the Scrap Parts as a secondary resource and allow the player to craft "random" parts from it. Sure, the whole decomposition system became much simpler. Still, in the end it solves the same problems with much more transparent and understandable approaches, which are easier to explain to the new player.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44897959/428a82d9f566a80518bf6847aec3ef0e35b0e69c.jpg"][/img][/p][p]So, many intricate features were either cut or simplified while keeping the main pillars of the game intact. And though I was sceptical at first, it gave me a boost in performance and motivation to move on. And the result of everything is the current version 0.7.0, which is - I still can't believe it - feature-complete.[/p][p]Many features are in the "prototype" state, but that was intentional. You can still play the game and feel every central gameplay system. It's impossible to win at the moment, and I need to address that next. But except for that, everything is, well, playable.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44897959/fbc7c705e9d8919985ed6d17418392ba7fdc2eda.jpg"][/img][/p][p]What is next? Polishing and content. Sure, everything "works", but it's still raw. Animations, effects, sound, UI and UX, variations, and so on - now it's time to start working on "everything else". My current plan is to get through the list of features again, but do a polishing iteration for everything to improve the overall experience. And after that - playtests, finally. I have a few internal playtesters, but I hope that soon will be the moment to show you the actual game and get your feedback.[/p][p]So, thank you for staying with me and stay tuned for more updates![/p][p][/p][p]I posted a few of the in-game screenshots in this article. You can notice that the visual style and the overall environment are also changed, but that's a story for another update. I think after everything is more polished, I'll provide both an updated trailer and the detailed change \\ feature list.[/p]

notes.title: Version 0.5.0 is live!
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

The new, major version of Synthetica: Cyber Club Manager is live. This is a huge milestone for the project because the core gameplay is here. You can craft and level up your Android workers, match them with clients' desires, buy new parts, participate in dialogues, and manage your club for days. This is amazing, but much work remains. We can switch our focus to content and secondary gameplay mechanics, such as research, boosts, perks, ratings, etc. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44897959/870257eb3f1428c79bb6a475a7c105c15d10347d.jpg[/img]

I hope we can start public playtests in a few months and that you will join us in the unique world of cyber club management!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44897959/f587bee98995619b750f7d93213852c04f2b27d5.jpg[/img]

[b]Changelist:[/b]
[list]
[*]A full-scale dialogue system with interactive events, stories, and results. Interact with your clients and help them solve their issues and problems.
[*]Reworked client interaction and overall behavior in the club. Clients can finally wait for the free spot and walk around the club. The overall interaction system is reworked to be more consistent and easier to understand
[*]Parts broker now sells parts to craft the new Androids
[*]Android creation system, craft components, skill leveling, and Android disassembly mechanics.
[*]New Day Result screen with graphs and improved readability
[*]Interactive "Conversation" events with clients, with Theme Selection and the overall base for "interaction mini-games" during the management phase.
[*]New animations for interactions
[*]Dancefloors (though it's a programmer's art at this stage)
[*]Reworked garbage cleanup and visualization
[*]Foundation for Research System
[*]Infinite bugfixes
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44897959/8f07aec338f5fcaf578fe6ac73cf26087e20808d.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Update v.0.4.6
notes.content:
The latest version of [i]Synthetica: Cyber Club Manager[/i] is live! This update brings some of our biggest changes yet as we continue building out the core gameplay systems and features. With new UI improvements, expanded android interactions, and the foundation of research mechanics, the game is getting closer to its full vision. Jump in and let us know what you think!

[b]Changelog:[/b]

[list]
[*] Reworked UI
[*] New Android Creation Screen
[*] Improved dialogue system
[*] Foundation for research mechanics
[*] New client interactions
[*] Android customization options
[*] Reworked camera system
[*] Various bugfixes and tweaks
[/list]

Don't forget to [b]wishlist the game[/b]!

notes.title: Version 0.4.3!
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

As you may have noticed, we switched from 2D pixel art to 3D. It was a hard decision, but overall, it would greatly improve both the quality of the game and the speed of development because our team's expertise in 3D is much higher.

Today we finally have a stable playable build with the new art style and reworked, well, everything? Most of the pixel-version legacy is gone (except for some icons and the overall UI) and the new 3d club, androids, and clients are already in the game.

notes.title: Version 0.3.0!
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

Version 0.3.0 of Synthetica: Cyber Club Manager is live on Steam! We had a bunch of internal builds between 0.2 and 0.3, but from now on, there will be more updates on Steam. We spent a lot of time finalizing the game's vision, features, and most UI mockups. Now we can move to the active production phase and I hope we'll be able to give access to the playtest build in a month or two.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44897959/0ab3331d422e7a9618d2172af847dbe3cae5028b.png[/img]

[b]Changelog:[/b]
[list]
[*] Skills for your androids!
[*] News generation system
[*] Another UI overhaul. We redesigned every screen and laid the ground for future UI implementation.
[*] New indication for available actions
[*] Reworked client queue
[*] The player can now open and close the club to control the number of clients
[*] The player can finish the interactions with current clients at the end of the day
[*] Rent payment is now every 3 days, not each day as before
[*] Lots of fixes in UI, AI and core systems
[/list]

Stay tuned for more updates and don't forget to wishlist the game!

notes.title: Version 0.2.0!
notes.content:
Finally, a major update version! We're slowly moving forward both with the visual style and the overall gameplay loop. The base for the game is here, but a lot of things should be improved and deepened. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44897959/e9cfc957515a3fbd1ef57f9e8b98018d1916a55b.png[/img]

[b]Changelog[/b]
[list]
[*] Reworked visual style for the club interior. Still WIP, but now it's way closer to the desired state and quality
[*] New android girls
[*] Infinite AI and flow tweaks
[*] "Easy" clients who only need some basic entertainment or drinks
[*] Reworked garbage and cleanliness logic
[*] UI tweaks (animation, states, overall UX)
[*] Bugfixes
[/list]

notes.content:
